hints._doc: Prompt fragments that belong to SEVERAL channels, stored once and referenced by `fetch_fallback_hint_ref`. A channel may also carry `fetch_fallback_hint` inline. 🔴 SINCE 2026-08-08 THERE IS ONE ACTIVE HINT (`mcp_fallback`), not two - see `_generalised_2026_08_08` below for why. The two-homes trap this key used to warn about is now closed by having ONE key rather than one-per-CLI; the `_why` and `_first_reading` notes below are HISTORY of the superseded design, kept because their measurements still frame what the merged hint is and is not doing.
hints.mcp_fallback:
## If a page will not open

You have MCP tools available in this session for reading web pages, and they are usually stronger than a plain fetch. When a page returns 403, 404, a CAPTCHA, a Cloudflare interstitial, an empty body or a JavaScript-only shell, do NOT give up and do NOT answer from memory. Look at the MCP tools you have available RIGHT NOW - some CLIs load tools lazily and you must issue a tool search first before you can see them - and try whichever one fits the failure. Say in your answer which tool finally worked.

Do NOT fetch or parse a page with the shell (`curl`, `wget`, `python -c`, one-off scripts) unless you have already verified the shell works in this environment. On many CLIs the shell path is either denied by policy (in which case one denied call may discard the whole run) or unable to spawn a subprocess at all - either way, a shell attempt in those cases costs you the run without returning a page. The MCP tools do not go through the shell.

Do NOT use billing-heavy fetchers - anything that bills per page or per token with no ceiling. Prefer free tools; use a metered scrape only as a last resort for a single page. If your session offers a whole-site crawler or an unbounded page-extraction agent, treat those as the meter you are asked to avoid, whatever they are named.

If everything fails, write that the page could not be opened, name what you tried, and tag the claim `[SNIPPET]` or `my search found no confirmation`. A host that refuses automated traffic has given an answer; do not try to defeat it.
hints._generalised_2026_08_08: 🔴 2026-08-08, the operator: «просто скажи, что бы он использовал MCP, а какие именно, не надо, ведь какой-то MCP мог зависнуть и в этот момент не загрузился». Sharper than the earlier «one CLI's tool list differs from another's» that had two paragraphs living where one should have. Availability is DYNAMIC, not static: a server present at install time can be hung, unloaded or filtered out by permissions when the actual call happens - and a named-but-absent tool makes the model report OUR error as its own. That is the same trap that produced the 2026-08-08 morning `NONE` reading for codex, one layer down. The two old paragraphs (`agy_mcp_fallback`, `codex_mcp_fallback`) are GONE; their measurement history is preserved in the `_why` and `_first_reading` notes below, and those notes are now archaeology - the current hint is `mcp_fallback` above, and it names ZERO tools. The three refs `agy31pro.fetch_fallback_hint_ref`, `agy36flash.fetch_fallback_hint_ref` and `codex.fetch_fallback_hint_ref` all now point to `mcp_fallback`. 🔴 THIS CHANGES THE PAYLOAD OF THE ROUND-27 RE-RUN EXPERIMENT: the hint whose effect is being measured is now the merged one, not the old codex or agy versions. Run it BEFORE trusting any conclusion about hint efficacy, on agy AND codex.
hints._codex_mcp_fallback_why: 🔴 SUPERSEDED 2026-08-08 by the merger noted above - kept because the CODE OF THE HINT is gone but the MEASUREMENTS are still true and still frame what the merged hint means. 🔴🔴 SUPERSEDES THE 2026-08-08 MORNING CONCLUSION THAT CODEX HAS NO MCP TOOLS. That conclusion came from asking the model («name your MCP page-reading tools») and taking `NONE` as a measurement. It was wrong, and the cause is worth more than the correction: codex-cli 0.147 loads tools LAZILY - the model sees them only after issuing a `tool_search_call` - so «what tools do you have?» is answered from an empty list unless it searches first. Asking a model to enumerate its own tools measures its discovery behaviour, not its tool set. RE-MEASURED the same day, by execution and by the client's own event log rather than by the model's word: `codex mcp list --json` reports NINE configured servers, all `enabled: true`; a probe run produced `mcp_tool_call_end {server: scrapling, tool: fetch}` -> `Ok`, and a second produced `{server: crawl4ai, tool: crawl_url}` -> `Ok`, both returning the real `<h1>` of example.com. 🔴 THE FIRST RE-PROBE WAS ALSO WRONG, in the same direction: after ONE tool search the model reported 3 servers / 20 tools and stated that jina «does not expose read_url». After eleven searches it reported 10 namespaces and 51 tools INCLUDING `read_url` - the first number was the search's `limit`, not the machine's. So even a probe that calls a tool successfully can enumerate the rest wrongly; the enumeration is a self-report at every depth, and only the `mcp_tool_call_end` frames are evidence. That is why the merged hint's first paragraph is about searching rather than about any particular tool. 🔴 Codex also carries `mcp__codex_apps__*` servers (github, tavily_ai, sites) that are NOT in ~/.codex/config.toml - vendor-side apps. They are deliberately not named in the hint: they were seen once, in one model's enumeration, which by the paragraph above is not evidence.
hints._agy_mcp_fallback_why: 🔴 SUPERSEDED 2026-08-08 by the merger noted above - kept for the anti-shell measurement, which is the paragraph the merged hint still carries. 2026-08-08, the operator: «может agy и codex писать доп. текст в промт, что бы они использовали MCP разные для открытия сайтов, если их встроенный fetch не смог открыть сайт?» — YES for agy, and 🔴 YES FOR CODEX TOO since the re-measurement recorded in `_codex_mcp_fallback_why` (the first answer here said NO, on the strength of the model's own `NONE`; that was a self-report, not a measurement, and it was wrong). The old two hints stayed SEPARATE rather than shared because tool names differed, the discovery model differed and the anti-shell paragraph had a different CAUSE on each (agy: a denied command discards the whole run; codex: the sandboxed shell cannot spawn PowerShell at all). 🔴 The 2026-08-08 evening merger reversed that: names dropped, generic wording covers both discovery paths, and the anti-shell paragraph covers both causes in one sentence («denied by policy OR unable to spawn») because dodging shell is the right advice under either. 🔴 The six servers named in the old agy hint were read from ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/mcp.json, not recalled: scrapling, playwright, firecrawl, jina-mcp-server, crawl4ai, cloakbrowser. 🔴 THE ANTI-SHELL PARAGRAPH IS THE REAL PAYLOAD, and it is aimed at a measured failure, not at a hypothetical one: round 27 watched agy die THREE times on three DIFFERENT one-off `python -c` scripts, each denied, each discarding a run that had already made ~29 successful tool calls. The failure is the deep-researcher profile's habit of shelling a fresh script, not a missing page. 🔴 It also goes WITH the grain of a measurement already in this repo: an earlier instruction telling agy to AVOID MCP failed 5/5, because a server's own tool description outranks a system prompt. Pointing it AT the tools it is already pulled toward pushes the same lever the way it already moves - which is why this one is worth trying and that one was not. 🔴 Firecrawl is named ONLY to forbid the unbounded call: the operator's spend policy is enforced by a Claude Code PreToolUse hook, and that hook does not cover agy's own MCP client.
hints._first_reading_2026_08_08: 🟢 FIRST READING, CONSISTENT WITH THE HYPOTHESIS - and it is one reading, not a proof. Round 28, both agy channels, counted from their own stream-json: agy31pro used 2 tools (both search_web); agy36flash used 14 (6 search_web, 4 view_file, 4 call_mcp_tool). `run_command` count: ZERO on both, and both returned status SUCCESS with a full answer - where round 27 had every attempt die on a denied one-off `python -c`. 🔴 WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH, and the distinction is the whole point: THE BRIEF CHANGED TOO. Round 27's brief was about packages and registries and provoked scripted downloads; round 28's was a design review that did not. Two variables moved, so the honest claim is «no shelling occurred and MCP was used four times», never «the hint prevented shelling». Isolating it costs one round: re-run round 27's brief WITH the hint. Do that before trusting this paragraph. 🔴 It does already correct round 27's other conclusion, that «agy31pro is unusable headless» - it ran fine here, so the failure was never the model.

groups._doc: A word a human types that means SEVERAL channels. Without these, splitting agy into two channels would have broken `--only agy` and «не используй gemini» with 'unknown channel' - the exact defect that made `--only http` unusable for weeks in 2026-07. A group is expanded by routing before anything else runs, so every flag and every free-text route accepts it. Group names and their aliases share one namespace with channel and model aliases, and a collision is refused at load time.

orgpt56terrapro._search_is_a_token_bomb:
🔴🔴 THE MOST EXPENSIVE CHANNEL IN THIS REGISTRY BY A WIDE MARGIN: TWO LIVE HARNESS RUNS BILLED $1.7641 AND $1.8071 FOR ONE REVIEW OF A 2 744-CHARACTER BRIEF. That is roughly 7x kimik3's ~$0.26 and it is not an anomaly - the two runs were consecutive, on the identical brief, and agreed within 3%. 🔴 AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS VERY NOTE PREDICTED «around $0.25» FROM SYNTHETIC PROBES AND WAS WRONG BY 7x; the number here is what the vendor reported through the harness, not an extrapolation, and it is written over the estimate rather than beside it.

WHY. Search and page-fetch text is re-sent on every later tool round, so the input bill is roughly quadratic in the number of rounds, not linear in the brief. Run 1: in=6,643,398 tokens (3,324,849 of them cache reads) for a 2.7 KB brief. Run 2: in=5,569,499 (3,969,070 cached). The isolated probes that produced the 50x figure below were real but far too small to reveal this: one native search on a 160-character question moved 1,754 prompt tokens / $0.0027 to 89,605 / $0.0557, and other arms reached 112-115K. A full review does that eight times over, on top of each other.

WHAT ACTUALLY DRIVES IT, both runs, same page: the model fetched `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models` - OpenRouter's ENTIRE model catalogue - to answer a question about ONE model. It came back at 399,995 chars, i.e. truncated at the 400 KB FETCH_MAX_BYTES ceiling, roughly 99k tokens, and was then re-sent on every subsequent round. The harness's oversized-page warning fired correctly both times; the cumulative FETCH_RUN_BUDGET did not, because the run total (~470 KB) stays under its 1 MB ceiling. So the guard that exists is aimed at a different failure than the one this channel produces.

NOT «FIXED» HERE, AND THAT IS A DECISION RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT. The obvious levers - lower fetch_tool.max_calls, or a per-channel page-size cap - both buy money with grounding, and grounding is the whole reason this channel earns its seat: it answered 4/4 on a brief with three planted falsehoods, every claim [OPENED] with verbatim quotes. Round 36 proposed exactly this shape of trade on the grok channel («cap reasoning or lower max_tokens») and the operator rejected the direction outright: «фокус на качество, а значит токенов на размышление урезать не надо». Capping this channel unasked would repeat that mistake. The cost is therefore MEASURED, WRITTEN DOWN, and left for a human to price - which is this project's own rule that a cost which does not appear in the plan is a cost nobody declined.

FLOOR AND CLIFF, both real: even a six-word question bills ~1,500-1,750 prompt tokens here, so the model carries substantial invisible scaffolding; and the 272,000-token high-context threshold in _catalogue (input rate doubles to $2/M, output to $9/M) is genuinely reachable on a multi-fetch round, which is true of no other channel in this registry.

The number it can read off a page is stable; the number it has to infer from page furniture is not. Treat its dates as [SNIPPET] unless the run's citation audit resolved them.

_panels_doc:
🔴 A PANEL IS WHO IS IN THE ROOM. A TIER IS HOW DEEP EACH OF THEM GOES. Added 2026-08-15 (round 42), the operator: «Давай теперь разделим оркестр[ацию] на дешевую и стандартную», with the membership he dictated verbatim - «В дешевую добавь: deepseek, Grok, Agy, google и openrouter 3.6 и 3.7 Flash, mimo, nemotron, spark12cont Muse Spark 1.2 Contributor». Everything he did not name stays standard-only: spark11, codex, kimik3, qwen38max, orgpt56terrapro. The two axes are deliberately orthogonal and both print in the plan - `--panel cheap --tier deep` is a legal and sensible combination (few reviewers, each thinking hard), and so is `--panel standard --tier strategic`.

🔴 THE LADDER IS NESTED, NOT A PARTITION: `standard` INCLUDES every cheap channel. «Стандартная» has to mean «what normally runs», and what normally runs is every enabled channel - so `--panel standard` is bit-for-bit the behaviour that shipped before this key existed, and the default is unchanged. A disjoint reading would have produced a four-channel «standard» panel with no Gemini voice at all, which nobody would ever want: the cheap voices cost nothing extra once you are already paying for the expensive ones.

🔴 A PANEL IS NOT A GROUP, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS RESURRECTION. `--only <group>` deliberately overrides `enabled: false` - that is the documented opt-in path. A panel must NOT: it filters DOWN to channels that are already enabled and never turns one on. Implementing `cheap` as a group instead would have been a one-line registry edit and would have been wrong in a way nothing would have caught, because `enabled` is exactly what package.py flips per `distribution`: `--only cheap` in the kit would have resurrected mimo25pro, grok420 and goog36/37flash - four channels whose direct vendor keys a kit user does not have - and here it would have resurrected their OpenRouter twins, paying twice for the same voice. Same word, opposite semantics; they cannot share a mechanism.

🔴 THE NAME `standard` WAS A TIER UNTIL 2026-08-08 AND IS NOT ONE NOW. the operator removed the `quick` and `standard` TIERS that day, and `--tier standard` is still an argparse error naming strategic|deep. The word returning as a PANEL is not that tier coming back - different flag, different axis. Recorded here because the retired name appears in `_tiers_doc` above and a reader meeting both would otherwise be entitled to think one of them is stale.
_panels_hidden_cost_doc: 🔴 THE THING THE CHEAP PANEL COSTS IS VENDOR DIVERSITY, NOT DEPTH - and it is invisible if you only read the price. Counted on this machine 2026-08-15: of the 11 cheap channels enabled here, SIX are Gemini (agy31pro, agy36flash, agy37flash, goog36flash, goog37flash, orgemini37flash). In the generated kit it is five of ten. A panel's whole product is disagreement between independent voices, and six seats sharing one vendor's training data are not six independent voices on a question where that vendor is systematically wrong - they will agree with each other and the convergence will read as corroboration. What `standard` actually buys, therefore, is not «more expensive», it is four more VENDORS: OpenAI (codex), Moonshot (kimik3), Alibaba (qwen38max) and Meta's Standard tier (spark11). The plan prints the vendor breakdown of whatever set resolves, so this is checkable at run time rather than trusted from this paragraph.
_default_panel_is_standard_ON_PURPOSE: Flipping this to "cheap" is a one-word edit and was deliberately NOT made in round 42. The reason is not caution in general, it is a specific asymmetry: making the default cheaper silently removes codex, kimik3, qwen38max and spark11 from every round launched by a session that passes no flag - including the legal rounds in another project, where the loss would be four vendors on a question with a filing deadline, and where nobody would see a message saying so. A default that quietly spends more is a bug; a default that quietly reviews LESS is also a bug, and the second one is harder to notice. So the change is offered rather than taken: every `standard` plan prints what `--panel cheap` would drop, by name.

cheap._aliases_and_the_two_things_that_are_NOT: «дешёвая» needs no entry: both the panel extractor and the entity scanner fold ё to е before matching, the same normalisation the route parser has always used. Case endings DO need entries, because nothing stems Russian here - «дешевой» is not derivable from «дешевая» by any rule this file implements. 🔴 WHAT A MISSING ENDING ACTUALLY DOES, CORRECTED 2026-08-15 after a reviewer traced it: this note used to say it «falls through to default_panel», which is only half the story and the reassuring half. If the rest of the route names a channel («не используй grok на дешевом»), the panel word is invisible and the round runs the DEFAULT - i.e. the expensive - panel, silently. If it names nothing («запусти на дешевом»), the route dies with «no channel or model in this route matched the registry», an error about the wrong thing entirely. Neither outcome is the one asked for, and one of them costs money. That is why this list is longer than it looks like it needs to be, and why the endings a Russian speaker would actually type were added by asking a panel rather than by introspection.
cheap._what_it_is: Every channel that is either free, on a flat-rate subscription, or metered below roughly $1/M input. Subscriptions (agy) count as cheap because their marginal cost is zero, even though the weekly allowance is a real and scarce resource - which is why `codex`, also a subscription, is NOT here: it is rationed for a different reason (slow, strategic-only), and that policy predates this key.
cheap._the_seat_it_loses: kimik3 carries `role: code` and is standard-only, so the cheap panel would have had no code voice at all. ordeepseekv4pro was added in the same round and carries `role: code` for exactly that reason. See _panels_hidden_cost_doc for the loss that is NOT filled by anything: four vendors.

standard.label: standard panel
standard.🔴_words_that_could_mean_DEPTH_are_not_pa: `full`, `полная`, `полную`, `полной` were here and are GONE, and the reason is sharper than «too common». A bare word is dangerous as a panel alias exactly when it could equally name the OTHER axis: «run a full analysis», «полная проверка» are asking for THOROUGHNESS, which is `--tier deep`, not for a room full of reviewers. Measured 2026-08-15, before the removal: `--route "run a full analysis with grok"` silently set panel=standard AND swallowed the word, so the leftover produced «'run a  analysis with grok' mentions grok420 but no instruction word» - the wrong action taken, and an error message about something else. `full panel` and `полная панель` stay, because the noun disambiguates. Two reviewers found this independently. The general rule for anyone adding an alias here: ask whether the word could be an answer to «how deep», not just whether it is common.
standard._what_it_is: Every enabled channel - the behaviour that shipped before panels existed, and the default. Adds spark11 (Meta Standard tier, no training grant), codex (OpenAI via the ChatGPT subscription, strategic questions only), kimik3 (Moonshot, the code voice) and qwen38max (Alibaba). orgpt56terrapro is nominally in this panel and still does not run without `--only` plus `--accept-spend`: `panel` and `enabled` answer different questions, and a panel never resurrects a default-off channel.

_tiers_doc: 🔴 TWO TIERS SINCE 2026-08-08, and the reason is a question that had no good answer. the operator: «quick и standart tier давай уберем. И не понятно визуально, чем отличается strategic от Deep.» He was right, and the honest answer was embarrassing: strategic and deep differed by NOTHING except a timeout - identical agy_effort, identical http_effort - so a human reading the two words was promised a depth difference the file did not contain. Rather than invent one, `deep` now changes the three things that CAN change on every vendor (time, pages read, room to think) and the plan PRINTS the resolved value per channel, including «already at this vendor's ceiling, deep changes nothing here». A tier is a word; what it resolves to has to be visible before anything is spent. 🔴 quick and standard are GONE, not hidden: `--tier quick` is now an argparse error naming the two that exist, because a silently-accepted dead tier is the decorative-knob defect this file keeps recording. 🔴 THE TIER LIST HAS ONE HOME. Until 2026-08-08 it had two - this object AND a `TIERS` dict in orchestrate.py that fed `--tier`'s choices - so deleting a tier here would have left the flag still accepting it and falling through to defaults. orchestrate now derives its tiers from this file. HISTORY, kept because each entry is a lever that was wired to nothing: codex_timeout added 2026-08-05 (before it, codex fell through to a hard-coded 3000 s while the harness advised 'raise the timeout for that channel', naming a lever that did not exist); http_effort added 2026-08-06 (the tier varied `thinking.budget_tokens`, which Meta documents as «accepted for compatibility but not translated into an effort value» - depth is output_config.effort alone, which the code pinned at xhigh for every tier, so the ladder did nothing on Spark). PROBED 2026-08-06 on both Spark models: low/medium/high/xhigh all return 200, `max` returns 400 on both, and so does an invented value - the negative control proving the endpoint validates the field. xhigh is the real ceiling even though Meta's own OpenAPI enum lists `max`.
_tiers_reach_correction_2026_08_15: 🔴 «AND EVERY OPENROUTER/OAI CHANNEL (REASONING CEILING AND PAGE-FETCH BUDGET, BOTH MULTIPLIED)» IN THE NEXT KEY IS TOO STRONG, and three of eight reviewers caught it on the same day. The multiplier acts on `reasoning.max_tokens`; a channel that declares `reasoning.effort` INSTEAD has no number to multiply, so `deep` moves only its fetch budget. That is true today of `ordeepseekv4pro` (effort high, two rungs) and of `ornemotron3ultra` (effort high). The plan has always printed the truth per channel - «nothing this tier can raise on this channel» - so the code was right and the prose generalised. Kept as a correction beside the original rather than edited into it, because the original sentence is the measurement of 2026-08-08 and rewriting a measurement to match a later one is how a record stops being a record. The fix that would make the sentence true again is a raise-only effort rule clamped to each model's declared ladder; deferred, because an absolute tier effort would silently DOWNGRADE qwen38max, which already runs xhigh.
_tiers_reach_doc: 🔴 WHICH CHANNELS THE TIER ACTUALLY REACHES, measured 2026-08-08 rather than assumed. Before this round the answer was 4 of 11 - two Spark and two agy - while `--tier` read like a global control. Now: agy (effort+timeout), codex (timeout only; its effort is pinned in its own block and the subscription has no cheaper setting worth having), http/Spark (effort+thinking budget+output floor), gemini (thinking_level - see goog36flash, this was believed impossible until the docs were re-read), and every openrouter/oai channel (reasoning ceiling and page-fetch budget, both multiplied). xai gets the timeout and nothing else. 🔴🔴 TWO CORRECTIONS TO THAT LAST CLAUSE, both from the round-29 panel reviewing this very change, and both right. (a) codex noticed the dispatcher passed NO timeout to the xai channel at all - `call_xai_responses` fell back to its own 2400 s default in both tiers - so `deep` was a literal NO-OP there while the printed note claimed it bought wall-clock. A line written to be honest about a missing lever was itself wrong about the one lever that remained. Fixed: it now takes `codex_timeout`. (b) qwen38max objected that «no depth knob on this vendor» rested on a single 400 from a single placement - the exact error this round had just corrected for Gemini - and cited xAI's own docs showing `reasoning_effort` on grok-4.5 and `reasoning.effort` on grok-4.20-multi-agent. RE-PROBED on /v1/responses in the Responses shape: `reasoning:{"effort":"low"|"high"|"zzz"}` ALL return `400 Model grok-4.20-0309-reasoning does not support parameter reasoningEffort`, identical to the top-level placement, while the invented sibling `reasoning:{"effort_zzz":"low"}` returns 200 and is silently ignored. The refusal is MODEL-level, not a placement mistake, so the correct wording is «this model», never «this vendor». The objection was methodologically right and changed the sentence even though it did not change the outcome - which is what a panel is for.

strategic._what_it_is: The default. Every vendor at the depth it supports, and enough time for a normal review. These are exactly the values that ran before the two-tier change, so switching to it costs nothing new.
strategic._gemini_thinking_level_note: Raised medium->high on 2026-08-08 at the operator's instruction, after measuring it rather than before (see goog36flash._thinking_level_default: medium 1635 thought tokens against high 1963, non-overlapping ranges over 3 interleaved samples each). This is the ONE tier value that is deliberately not «what ran before»: thought tokens bill as output on this channel, so the default tier now costs about 20% more thinking here. It also means `high` is the enum ceiling on BOTH tiers, and `deep` therefore has nothing left to raise on this channel - which the plan says out loud rather than omitting.

deep._what_it_is: More TIME, more READING, more ROOM TO THINK - deliberately not «more effort», because on four of the seven vendors strategic is already at the ceiling and there is nowhere above it. Concretely: agy 25m->40m, codex 50m->75m, Spark thinking budget 60k->100k and output floor 15k->25k, Gemini thinking_level medium->high, every OpenRouter/MiMo channel's reasoning ceiling and page-fetch budget DOUBLED. That last line is the one that costs money: doubling the fetch budget doubles the pages a channel may pull into its context, and context is what OpenRouter bills.
